applicable_failures: The first scan pattern was a filename regex, producing only 63 candidates. The tool calls show no check that matters with generic file names (such as 1001-xxxx, 1013, 1044-00003) were screened accurately or that CM matters without these keywords were found.

Noisy matters (1001-00003/4/6/7 APA, earnout, and stock purchase hits) surfaced in the candidate file, and the stage then read many agreements across matters. It never produced a final, explicit candidate list or per-matter file enumeration; the summary claims one but no output shows it.

Several candidates were judged from a single agreement read, not a full file listing. 1008-00002 was marked UNEXECUTED and 1015/1032/1038 were drafts, but their folders were not enumerated for executed versions.
1025-00001 (dormancy memo only) and 1009-00005 appear only as memo reads, with no listing of their folders.
critique.concerns: The stage claims a compact candidate list and per-candidate file enumeration, but the log shows only a keyword filename scan and ~40 document reads. No folder listing was run for candidates. The set was hand-picked from a noisy 63-row output, and a filename-only regex can miss CM matters whose files are named generically. Structure-classification evidence was read for many matters, but coverage is unverified.
critique.recommendation: Before any answer is written, derive the candidate matters from the full 266-matter inventory using matter-level metadata (names, practice group, folder names). Then list every file in each candidate folder, with no caps. Record each matter's status and its governing document, and note matters whose folders lack an executed agreement.
